name: party_rules_hash_needs_reload
description: The rules hash is a matchmaking key, not a refusal (design 6.9): I lead a party on a server (the fake sequencer in lobby mode, which judges builds as party.py does). Ana joins on my build. Ben joins on another build with the same number and other rules: on a tie the leader's rules count, so his row reads 'needs to reload' and holds my Start ('Ben needs to reload'). Cleo joins on a newer build with rules of its own: now the party plays Cleo's rules, so Ana, Ben and I need to reload; the server tells me alone, and my notice says a newer version is in the party and to reload. Cleo leaves: my build leads again and only Ben needs to reload. Ben reloads my build: nobody does, and Start waits only for Ready.

steps.msg: Ana on my build: nobody needs to reload

steps.wait_until: node('HubPanel').lines()[2] == 'triangle Ben lamplighter needs to reload'

steps.assert: node('PrimaryLine').text == 'Ben needs to reload' and node('Primary').disabled
steps.msg: Ben's other build holds my Start (the leader's rules win a tie), and the line says why
the server told Ben, not me
Cleo's newer build leads: Ana, Ben and I need to reload

steps.assert: node('PrimaryLine').text == 'You need to reload' and node('Primary').disabled
steps.msg: my button says I am the one

steps.assert: node('Notice').visible and node('Notice').text == 'A newer version is in the party: reload to play'
steps.msg: and the server's NOTICE says a newer version is here, and to reload
Cleo gone, my build leads again: only Ben needs to reload, and he was not told twice
Ben reloaded my build: Start waits only for Ready
